items.t: Said a law making contraceptives easier to access would help protect women's health and let women keep control over their own bodies and lives.
items.q: This law will make it easier for women to access contraceptives to prevent pregnancy from happening in the first place, which is one of the best ways to help women maintain control over their own bodies and their lives.

items.t: Worked with local organizations to fight against the PennEast Pipeline.
items.q: She has worked with local organizations to fight against the PennEast Pipeline, a natural gas pipeline that threatens our water supply and natural resources.

items.t: Initially opposed a bill over its potential rate hikes and giveaways, and said her colleagues convinced her the state had no one to bid on the energy incentives.
items.q: State Sen. Shirley Turner (D-Mercer) had initially opposed the bill over its potential rate hikes and giveaways, but said her colleagues convinced her the New Jersey government “didn’t have anybody to bid” on the energy incentives.

items.t: Said a resource guide would help hearing parents of deaf children understand their children's needs and the services available, and would introduce them to the deaf community.
items.q: Providing them with a resource guide will help parents better grasp the needs of their children and the services available to them. It will also help introduce parents to the deaf community which can provide support and guidance for the children and their loved ones.
